strategy.summary: Reproduce the npy_gcd INT_MIN abs-overflow defect in NumPy at the buggy commit b2b53f3c4963 by building NumPy from source and running the developer's test_gcd_overflow. The test should fail on the buggy build and pass on the fixed build, but only where the UB actually manifests (reported on s390x with GCC 11.5 -O2 -march=z14). On x86-64 or newer GCC the transition may not occur, and that is a known risk, not something this plan can guarantee.

system_packages: gcc (version matching reporter if available, reported GCC 11.5)
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy.git && cd numpy && git checkout b2b53f3c4963 && git submodule update --init
python -m pip install meson-python ninja Cython pytest hypothesis
git checkout <fixed-parent-or-fix-commit> then rebuild with the same command to get the fixed build
pinned_because: numpy source pinned to buggy commit b2b53f3c4963 (the evidence names this commit explicitly)
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README Testing section but carry no version constraint, so latest compatible versions are used
python version is not stated by the evidence (null); NumPy at this era requires a modern CPython, so use the version the buggy commit's pyproject.toml requires
CFLAGS -O2 mirrors the reporter's optimization level; -march=z14 only applies on s390x and is not assumed elsewhere
numpy version 2.4.4 from issue#31359 is the reporter's runtime, not a build constraint, so it is not pinned

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py::TestRationalFunctions::test_gcd_overflow (updated in the PR to loop over int8, int16, int32, int64 and to test INT_MIN as both first and second argument)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy b2b53f3c4963 built on s390x with GCC 11.5 -O2: test_gcd_overflow FAILS, because np.gcd(INT_MIN, q*3) returns -536870912 rather than q=536870912 for int32 and/or int64. On the fixed build (unsigned abs via utype): test_gcd_overflow PASSES for all four dtypes and both argument orders. The transition is the outcome of this single test; no separate value check is required.
risks: Platform dependence: the defect was reported only on s390x with GCC 11.5 -O2 -march=z14 and reported not reproducible on other architectures or later GCC versions. On x86-64 the buggy build may pass test_gcd_overflow, giving no transition. Run on s390x or a matching toolchain to get a real fail-to-pass result.

Signed-overflow UB: the observed value depends on compiler optimization. -fwrapv masks the bug per the issue, so do not build the buggy revision with -fwrapv or the test will pass for the wrong reason.
Sanitiser sensitivity: UBSan would flag the overflow, but a sanitiser build is not stated in the evidence and is not assumed here.
The int8 and int16 additions in the test likely pass even on buggy code, because C promotes those operands to int before negation; the int32 and int64 cases carry the transition.
The fixed-build environment is not stated by the evidence (PR claims PASS but gives no platform), so the fixed-side result is inferred from the patch, not observed.
The provided test_commands are unreliable: 'numpy.test()' is not a dependable NumPy entry point and the second command is a one-liner, not the project test; the pytest command above is used instead.
Dependencies pytest and hypothesis are documented but unbounded, so a newer release than the PR era could change collection behaviour; this is a chosen default, not an evidence-backed constraint.

oracle.reference_source: assert_equal(np.gcd(a, q*3), q) in test_umath.TestRationalFunctions.test_gcd_overflow; expected value is the mathematically correct non-negative gcd q
oracle.why: gcd is an integer function and the expected result is exact, so an exact comparison applies with no tolerance

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On s390x GCC 11.5 -O2, the buggy npy_gcd computes abs(INT_MIN) with signed overflow, so assert_equal sees -536870912 where q=536870912 is expected, and the assertion fails. On x86 this may not occur and the test may pass, so the failure is architecture-dependent.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the fix, abs is computed in unsigned arithmetic (utype), so gcd(INT_MIN, 3q) returns q for every tested dtype and argument order, and assert_equal succeeds.
